My research examines how climate shocks, market constraints, technology adoption, and policy interventions affect agricultural productivity, food security, and the welfare and resilience of farm households. Using household survey data, agricultural data, and climate and conflict-event data, I apply econometric methods, causal inference, and impact evaluation to address policy- and program-relevant questions in agricultural and development economics. My work contributes to understanding agricultural and rural development challenges, with implications for policy design and program implementation.

### Recent Work

**[Climate Shocks, Household Food Security and Welfare in Afghanistan](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.foodpol.2025.102910)**
<br>Ahmadzai, H., and Morrissey, O. *Food Policy*, 2025. Also presented at [Stanford University, April 2026](https://events.stanford.edu/event/climate-shocks).

**[Crop Diversification and Farm Household Welfare during Conflict: Afghanistan 2011–2017](https://doi.org/10.1080/00220388.2024.2404576)**
<br>Ahmadzai, H., and Morrissey, O. *The Journal of Development Studies*, 2025, 61(3), 381–399.

**[Tests for Market Failures and Overcoming Transaction Costs Barriers to Market Participation in Afghanistan](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40847-024-00364-2)**
<br>Ahmadzai, H. *Journal of Social and Economic Development*, 2026, 28, 637–655.


### Research Interests
Agricultural & Food Policy • Climate Shocks, Adaptation, & Agricultural Resilience • Farm & Household Economics • Food Security and Rural Livelihoods • Applied Econometrics & Causal Inference
